item.title: Bomb found near ethanol plant in central Illinois forces evacuations
item.description:
National
Bomb found near ethanol plant in central Illinois forces evacuations
November 14, 20263:12 PM ET
By
The Associated Press
A bomb was found near an ethanol plant in central Illinois, sparking evacuations of those who live near the industrial site as law enforcement officials investigate, authorities said Saturday.
The bomb was found Friday afternoon at the BioUrja Renewables facility in Peoria. While officials say the device has since been "rendered safe," as of Saturday morning, all residents within a 1-mile radius remained under an evacuation notice as officials continued to scour the facility for any other bombs and evidence.
Meanwhile, shelters have been set up for those displaced by the threat, authorities said.
"This is a credible threat," Peoria Police Chief Brad Dixon told reporters just after midnight Saturday. "We need to take the blast radius seriously."
FBI Special Agent Ryan Pressley said his agency was investigating, but declined to provide further details.
"We will work tirelessly to identify the individual responsible and bring them to justice," he said.
No arrests have been made at this time and no injuries have been reported.
Peoria Mayor Rita Ali told WMBD-TV on Friday that BioUrja is "a plant that has ethanol and highly combustible types of chemicals, and so that's what alarms us."
It's not unusual for law enforcement to receive bomb threats and suspicious package calls, but they often don't result in a credible threat even though such calls are taken seriously by officials who must assess and investigate the claims.

A ballot measure that would have repealed Alaska's nonpartisan primary system and ranked choice voting has failed, according to an overnight race call by the Associated Press.
This is the second time Alaskans voted down an effort to repeal the state's unique election system, which voters first approved in 2020. A repeal effort in 2024 also failed narrowly.

Democrats are not in the majority yet, but the first post-election test of their ability to get things done was a failure.
The House was unable to advance an impeachment effort of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. Eleven Democrats were no-shows for the vote. Based on the math in this vote: If those 11 had been there and if no more Republicans showed up, the attempt would have gone forward.
Now, for those who want to see Hegseth impeached, it's fair to ask why only one Republican was in favor of it, Rep. item.title: Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins wins race for Alaska governor, replaces a Republican
item.description:

Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins wins race for Alaska governor, replaces a Republican
November 14, 202612:12 AM ET
From
By
Eric Stone
Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins, a Democrat, has won the race for governor of Alaska and will replace the outgoing Republican. Here he's seen at a polling station at the University of Alaska Anchorage on Election Day.
Eric Stone/Alaska Public Media
hide caption
toggle caption i
Eric Stone/Alaska Public Media
Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins, a former state representative from the small island community of Sitka, won the race for Alaska governor, according to a race call by the Associated Press. At 37, he'll be the youngest governor in state history.
Kreiss-Tomkins will replace outgoing Gov. Mike Dunleavy, a term-limited Republican who has been governor since 2018. The state's last Democratic governor was Tony Knowles, who left office in 2002.
Kreiss-Tomkins, known by his initials JKT, made his "high-energy, bipartisan, problem-solving approach" a centerpiece of his campaign.
